name: Glutathione face whitening

card.summary: Use of glutathione, taken by mouth, as a cream or intravenously, in the hope of lightening skin tone and giving a brighter, more even complexion.
card.note: Intravenous use for skin lightening is advised against by the Philippine government; side effects are reported.

quick.overview:
Glutathione is a small antioxidant molecule the body makes naturally. In beauty culture, particularly in parts of Asia, it is marketed as a way to lighten skin and even tone, either as supplements, creams or drips and injections given in clinics.

Practitioners and clients say it produces a brighter complexion over a course of sessions. Published research on this use is limited, and a general reference notes that as of 2019 it was unclear whether it actually works.
quick.how: Forms include oral supplements, topical creams and intravenous infusions given in clinics, usually in a series of sessions. Users often combine them with sun protection and other brightening products.
quick.risks: The Philippine government recommends against intravenous use for whitening, and reported side effects of the IV route are noted in general references. Skin-lightening products in general can contain harmful ingredients such as mercury, hydroquinone and corticosteroids.

lead: Glutathione face whitening is the use of glutathione, a tripeptide the body makes as an antioxidant, to lighten skin tone and produce a brighter, more even complexion [1]. It is described as the most common agent taken orally to whiten skin and can also be used as a cream [2].

Light skin is widely regarded as beautiful in South Korea according to Wikipedia, and the popularity of Korean beauty products has helped spread whitening trends to other Asian countries [2]. Glutathione treatments are one of the options offered in clinics in this market.

Oral glutathione is reported to have poor bioavailability [1]. As of 2019, whether glutathione lightening actually works was described as unclear, and the Philippine government recommends against intravenous use [2].

chain: Glutathione given orally, topically or by drip
angle.text: Users take glutathione hoping for a lighter and more even face. The claimed route is reduced pigment production, though this is described as unclear in reference works.

infobox: Philippine government advises against IV use for whitening

paras: Glutathione is the most abundant low-molecular-mass thiol in most cell types and works as an antioxidant [1]. In cosmetic use it is promoted for brighter, lighter skin [2].

Skin whiteners as a category are illegal in various countries and can contain mercury, hydroquinone or corticosteroids [2]. The Philippine government recommends against intravenous glutathione for whitening [2].
